platform: Classic ESP32, Arduino-ESP32 3.3.7, ESP-IDF 87912cd291, Xtensa GCC 14.2.0
method: Read linked native Xtensa entry a1,N instructions for individual function frame reservations and verify synchronous call paths against source and disassembly.

Compile channel.cpp alone with the saved benchmark compiler arguments and -fstack-usage, both default and -DMLOG_roo_transport_reliable_channel_connection=1. The logging variant was not linked or flashed.
Read pxPortInitialiseStack, _xt_lowint1 and _frxt_int_enter in the same ELF to verify permanent coprocessor storage and task-stack interrupt context before the switch to port_IntStack.

evidence: pxPortInitialiseStack 0x40089fb3: physical stack top minus 96 for coprocessor storage; 0x4008a00f stores that reduced pointer as initial application A1.
_xt_lowint1 0x40083bec: saves a 192-byte context below current task A1.
_frxt_int_enter 0x4008a2e7 saves task SP in TCB; 0x4008a2e9 switches to port_IntStack.
ELF _thread_local_start equals _thread_local_end: no additional TLS section reservation in this build.

sender_handshake.condition: Connection MLOG enabled, default log prefix enabled, interrupt arrives during deepest pointer-formatting call.

receive_ack_warning.condition: Checksum-valid ACK with unexpected control bit triggers the default-enabled cross-talk LOG(WARNING); default log prefix enabled; interrupt arrives during deepest pointer-formatting call.

limits: These are lower bounds for particular reachable synchronous paths, not whole-program worst-case upper bounds or hardware measurements of these paths.
Additional helper calls, register spills, application callbacks, logging hooks, alternative backends and different compiler/SDK configurations can change stack requirements.
Logging text buffers and all framing/window arrays are heap allocations, not task-local arrays.
Firmware stack settings remain 4096 bytes; neither a 2048-byte nor 3072-byte worker configuration is validated by this static audit.
